newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hecklers call Herzog "traitor" over German border.
newsitem.headline: Hecklers call Herzog "traitor" over German border.

text.p: Hecklers shouted down German President Roman Herzog as a "traitor" on Sunday as he addressed people expelled from areas now part of Poland and Russia, saying those regions no longer belonged to Germany.
Herzog, interrupted during a speech before an annual gathering of expelled citizens, responded by saying: "You should be ashamed."
He made clear that Germany's eastern border with Poland is now fixed by international law and that the German government would not attempt to reclaim the land.

"These areas belong to our historical and cultural heritage, but they don't belong to our nation," Herzog said, to a smattering of boos from the crowd. "The reunited Germany will not raise any claims in the region."
As one man shouted that Herzog was "a traitor to our fatherland," the president stopped his speech and turned towards the man.
"That's all that is missing here," Herzog said. "I really don't need to take that from you. You should be ashamed of yourself!"

Herzog, who noted in his speech that more than 15 million Germans were expelled from their homelands in the east at the end of World War Two, also urged the German government to move forward with a long-delayed German-Czech reconciliation treaty.

Many German expellees have waged a tireless campaign to someday return to their lost homeland. They reject the Bonn government's decision to call Germany's current border with Poland -- formed by the Oder and Neisse rivers -- the nation's eastern border.

The expellees, although thinning in number as the years advance, are a politically powerful group that exerts considerable pressure in key areas such as Bavaria and Baden-Wuerttemberg, where many of the millions who were resettled in western Germany live.
